results.message: What did your bishops decide at Chalcedon about Christ's two natures?

voice_event.speaker: lpc
voice_event.text:
We were not at Chalcedon. That council met in 451, and our last bishop died in 430, while the Vandals stood outside his own city's walls. What happened after our years is not ours to tell.

What we can give you is what we held while we lived. To us, Jesus is God's only Son within the one Trinity. His death and rising are not facts we simply affirm and set aside. His crucifixion, his burial, his rising on the third day, his going up to the Father — all were ordered so that our own life could be cut to their shape. We crucify our own flesh: that is his cross in us. We are buried with him in the water: that is his burial in us. We walk in a life made new: that is his rising in us. That is his dying and rising, worked out in an ordinary life.

How the churches after us worded what he was in himself, using the language Chalcedon chose, belongs to their own years, not to ours.
